text.p: Ken Doherty became the first player from the Republic of Ireland to win the world professional snooker title on Monday, ruining Stephen Hendry's attempts to win the championship for a seventh time.
Doherty, 27, beat Hendry 18-12 in the final to end the Scottish champion's 29-match unbeaten record at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield and collect a winning cheque of 210,000 pounds ($340,000).
A former world amateur champion, Doherty had to endure some anxious moments in the final session when Hendry showed signs of a fightback having trailed 11-5 overnight.

But the world number one was unable to find the sort of form which has overwhelmed so many of his rivals in the past and, despite winning five frames in a row, could not claw his way back from 15-7 down.
Alex Higgins and Dennis Taylor have both claimed the world title for Northern Ireland in the past, but Doherty's triumph is only the second non-British victory after Canadian Cliff Thorburn.

"I'm delighted it's all over to be honest," said Doherty having taken the last three frames of the match. "All the family back home were nervous wrecks. I think they were all having nervous breakdowns.
"As for me, the butterflies were turning into pigeons they were getting so big."
Hendry, who had won the last five successive world championships, described his opponent as a "deserved winner", identifying the moment the final slipped away from him.
"I missed a red along the cushion for a chance to win the fourth frame of the evening. That was my chance gone after that," he said.
He still has a chance to become the first modern-day player to win seven world titles but, for the time being, the Scotsman's spell has been broken.
